data.name: Project VO2
data.tagline: An Open-Source Instrument for Metabolic Analysis (VO2, VCO2, RMR, VO2 Max)
data.mission: To collaboratively design and build a high-fidelity, open-source scientific instrument for personal research, achieving gold-standard accuracy.
data.thesis: By implementing a modern, distributed architecture that co-locates sensor-to-digital conversion in a dedicated front-end module and leveraging open-source collaboration, a community-driven project can create a metabolic analyzer with accuracy and resolution comparable to commercial gold-standard systems.

data.decision: Adopt a distributed architecture with a dedicated Sensor Front-End (SFE) microcontroller and a Host Processing Unit (HPU) single-board computer.
data.rationale: Separates hard real-time data acquisition from non-real-time high-level processing, ensuring signal integrity and system reliability. This is a modern, professional standard for embedded systems.

data.decision: Use C++ with the PlatformIO framework for the v1.0 SFE firmware.
data.rationale: The C++ ecosystem for our target microcontrollers (Teensy/ESP32) is vastly more mature than the embedded Rust ecosystem. This provides access to vendor SDKs, a larger talent pool, and a massive library of professional-grade drivers, directly supporting the goal of an accelerated timeline. A future port to Rust is a v2.0 goal.

data.decision: Use the Raspberry Pi 5 as the v1.0 HPU.
data.rationale: The RPi 5 offers the best balance of performance, cost, community support, and standardization for the HPU's role. Potential 'manual toil' will be eliminated via a professional DevOps workflow (Dev Containers, CI/CD).

data.decision: Do not adopt RISC-V SBCs for the v1.0 implementation.
data.rationale: While philosophically aligned, the RISC-V software and community ecosystem is not yet mature enough. Adopting it now would add significant R&D overhead and risk to the project timeline. RISC-V is a primary goal for a future v2.0.

data.decision: Do not integrate or use the apple/containers project.
data.rationale: The project is specific to the Swift ecosystem and offers no advantages for our established toolchain (Python, C++). It would add unnecessary complexity and serves no project goal.

data.decision: Leverage advanced AI models as a 'development copilot' for boilerplate code, debugging, and documentation assistance. Architect data logging to support future AI-driven data analysis (artifact detection, advanced filtering).
data.rationale: This is a low-risk, high-reward strategy to accelerate development without distracting from the core mission of direct measurement. Predictive AI models are out of scope for v1.0.

data.name: Evolutionary Governance Framework
data.roles_model: Hats-to-Roles evolution (Lead Integrator, EE, Firmware, Software, ME, Test)

data.v1_focus: Purely open-source, non-commercial, for personal research and educational use. Liability managed via formal disclaimer in project documentation.
data.future_considerations: Potential for seeking grants or corporate sponsorship (e.g., from RISC-V ecosystem players) after a successful v1.0 prototype is validated. This would represent a strategic shift requiring formal program management.

data.rationale: Separates the reusable governance frameworks from the specific product implementation, allowing independent evolution and enabling the broader community to use the frameworks for their own projects.

data.decision: Deprecate the 'DIY' term from the official project name and all public-facing documentation. Adopt 'Project VO2: An Open-Source Instrument' as the public title and rely on a formal, explicit disclaimer for liability management.
data.rationale: The term 'DIY' does not accurately reflect the professional standard of the project and is not the optimal term for attracting senior talent. A formal disclaimer provides a stronger and more professional liability shield.

data.decision: The official project name is 'Project VO2'. 'VO2 Max' will be used in the tagline for recognition but not in the formal name to maintain technical accuracy.
data.rationale: The instrument measures the VO2 process; VO2 Max is a derived metric. This distinction is important for accurately communicating with a professional scientific and engineering audience.
